title: Historical VOLT Language and Toolchain Review (pre-0.3.0)
scope: vcc.py: lexer, parser, type checker, code generator, and build driver
review_summary: Historical snapshot of VOLT before version 0.3.0. The findings below describe that earlier tree and must not be read as current defects. The review targets Linux x86-64; it never claimed generated programs were a sandbox.

implemented_language_safety: Fixed-array and string indexing are bounds-checked.
Integer arithmetic, integer conversions, and float-to-integer conversions trap on overflow or invalid range.
Raw-pointer operations and raw-pointer APIs require unsafe blocks or unsafe functions.
Standard output and error helpers report write failures instead of discarding them.
remaining_limits: Raw pointers inside unsafe code still have no runtime bounds or lifetime checks.
Safe string indexing rescans the NUL-terminated length; hot character loops should cache the length and use an unsafe raw-pointer loop.
The runtime and ABI remain Linux x86-64/System V only.

findings_status: All entries in findings and improvement_suggestions are historical observations from the pre-0.3.0 tree.

targeted_probes: Confirmed source-controlled linker text executes a shell command during compilation.
Confirmed panic("x") segfaults, an oversized array overwrites a prior local, and a huge string repeat segfaults.
Confirmed compound assignment evaluates an indexed target twice and module initialization observes stale dependency state.
Confirmed u64-to-f64 conversion, global float division, log2 repetition, integer printing, and exp(4.9) produce incorrect results.
Confirmed malformed indentation and duplicate struct definitions are accepted, len has broken arity handling, and uppercase RET can crash a native function.
checks.source_changes: No compiler, runtime, library, test, or documentation source was changed; the findings are recorded in review.json.

findings.title: Source-controlled linker text is executed by the shell
findings.evidence: The link directive is appended to a command string passed to os.system. A source directive like link "; touch /tmp/opencode/marker; #" created the marker during compilation.
findings.impact: Compiling an untrusted .volt file can execute arbitrary shell commands before the compiled program is run.
findings.recommendation: Never interpolate source-controlled link text into a shell command. Invoke tools with argument lists and shell=False, and either disallow link directives for untrusted builds or allowlist the supported linker options. Apply the same non-shell invocation to assembler and executable launch paths.

findings.title: panic writes a fixed length from the caller's message pointer
findings.evidence: VOLT_rt_panic uses .Lsc_len, the length of the static panic banner, as the write length for the supplied pointer. panic("x") segfaulted in a targeted run.
findings.impact: Short messages cause an out-of-bounds read; longer messages are truncated. The syscall may expose adjacent memory or fault.
findings.recommendation: Compute the supplied message length before write, or ignore the parameter and write only the static banner. Add tests for empty, short, and long messages.

findings.title: An oversized array initializer writes beyond the array
findings.evidence: The declared array length is stored, but code generation loops over every initializer element without checking its count. With let canary: i64 = 777 followed by let a: [2]i64 = [1, 2, 3], the extra element overwrote canary with 3.
findings.impact: A simple source-level length mismatch corrupts another local and can damage the stack frame.
findings.recommendation: Reject an initializer whose element count exceeds the declared array length before code generation. Keep zero-fill behavior only for missing elements if that is the intended language rule.

findings.title: String repeat length overflow bypasses the arena limit
findings.evidence: str_repeat calculates need = strlen(s) * n using signed i64, then str_arena_new checks a potentially overflowed sum. Repeating a two-byte string INT64_MAX times overflowed need to a negative value and segfaulted while writing before the arena.
findings.impact: An oversized repeat count can bypass the 1 MiB arena check and write outside the mapped buffer. mmap failure is also not checked before the pointer is used.
findings.recommendation: Check multiplication and addition for overflow before allocation, reject requests larger than remaining capacity, and validate mmap's return value before storing the arena pointer.

findings.title: Compound assignment evaluates its target twice
findings.evidence: The old value is read with expr_value(tg), then the destination address is recomputed with eaddr(tg). For a[next_index()] += 5, a side-effecting next_index is called once for the read and again for the write.
findings.impact: The value can be read from one element and written to another; calls and other side effects in the target run twice.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate the lvalue address once, save it in a temporary, load the old value through that address, and store the result through the same address.

findings.title: Module initializers run before their dependencies
findings.evidence: Modules are retained in recursive load order (importer before dependency), and init calls follow that order. A module a importing b can therefore run before b's initializer and observe b's default global value. The auto-loaded str module is appended after user modules, so a top-level str_concat or str_repeat call in a user module can run before str_arena_init.
findings.impact: Initialization results depend on import traversal order and may use uninitialized module state or panic during string operations.
findings.recommendation: Build an explicit dependency order and initialize dependencies before dependents, including automatically loaded standard modules. Detect or define behavior for import cycles.

findings.title: u64-to-f64 conversion uses signed conversion
findings.evidence: The conversion paths use cvtsi2sd/cvtsi2ss, which interpret the 64-bit source as signed. Casting u64 value 18446744073709551615 to f64 produced -1.0.
findings.impact: Values above INT64_MAX convert to negative floating-point values, including explicit casts, assignments, and float parameters.
findings.recommendation: Implement unsigned 64-bit integer-to-float conversion and use it consistently in casts, assignments, and call argument lowering.

findings.title: Mixed signed/unsigned comparisons depend on operand order
findings.evidence: For equal-width mixed-sign integers, num_widen selects the signedness of the left operand. With a = -1 as i64 and b = 1 as u64, a < b was true while b > a was false.
findings.impact: Swapping operands can change the comparison domain and break basic ordering identities.
findings.recommendation: Define one symmetric conversion rule for mixed signedness (or reject such operations unless explicitly cast) and use it for arithmetic and comparisons.

findings.title: Global constant folding disagrees with runtime typing and arithmetic
findings.evidence: fold_const uses integer-style truncation for division, so a global f64 initialized by 7.0 / 2.0 becomes 3.0. An explicitly typed global such as let x: i64 = true + 1 bypasses normal expression type checking and is folded to 2. Conversely, const_type accepts and/or as boolean operations but fold_const does not implement them, so true and false is rejected.
findings.impact: The same expression can behave differently in a local and a global initializer, and invalid or valid expressions are inconsistently accepted.
findings.recommendation: Type-check global expressions with the same semantic rules as function expressions, then fold according to the resolved types. Add parity tests for arithmetic, comparisons, and logical operators.

findings.title: The log2 intrinsic leaks x87 stack entries
findings.evidence: The common path loads x before the log2 branch; that branch then loads 1 and x again. fyl2x and the final fstp remove the result but leave the first x on the x87 stack. Repeated log2(2.0) calls eventually returned invalid values.
findings.impact: Repeated log2 calls, and library functions built on log2 such as ln and log10, become incorrect after the x87 stack fills.
findings.recommendation: Use a branch-specific x87 stack setup and verify that every intrinsic leaves the x87 stack at its entry depth. Add a repeated-call test.

findings.title: Array element types are not checked and array-valued initializers are discarded
findings.evidence: The array literal path calls tf for each item but never compares its type with the element type. A [1]i64 initialized with a string compiled and treated the string address as an integer. For let b: [2]i64 = a, the non-list initializer is discarded and b is zero-filled.
findings.impact: Invalid typed programs compile, and an apparently valid array copy silently loses its source value.
findings.recommendation: Check every item with can_assign. Either implement array copy initialization or reject non-list array initializers with a clear diagnostic.

findings.title: A block does not require indentation beyond its header
findings.evidence: parse_block takes the next token's indentation as the block baseline without comparing it with the parent statement. A body aligned with its if header is accepted as a body; the following statements can be swallowed into that body instead of rejected as malformed indentation.
findings.impact: Invalid indentation silently changes program structure and can suppress statements.
findings.recommendation: Pass the header indentation to parse_block, require a strictly greater indentation for non-inline blocks, and report inconsistent indentation explicitly.

findings.title: Uppercase RET bypasses the native-body check and corrupts the stack
findings.evidence: The parser rejects only lowercase ret/retq. The assembler accepts uppercase RET, but the compiler still appends its own epilogue. A native function ending in RET segfaulted in a targeted run because it returned before restoring its stack frame.
findings.impact: A case variation of a forbidden instruction makes a native function return through the wrong stack address.
findings.recommendation: Parse the native instruction mnemonic case-insensitively and reject all return aliases, or remove the fragile text check and validate native blocks more robustly.

findings.title: Integer exponent literals advance the lexer too far
findings.evidence: After consuming the integer prefix, the lexer advances by len(text), which includes that already-consumed prefix. The valid expression print(1e2+3) skips the plus and fails to parse; malformed 1e can also raise an uncaught Python exception because the exponent match is not checked.
findings.impact: Valid exponent expressions can fail, while malformed input can produce a Python traceback instead of a compiler diagnostic.
findings.recommendation: Advance only by the exponent suffix length and turn missing exponent digits into a VErr. Add compact and whitespace-separated exponent tests.

findings.title: len does not enforce exactly one argument
findings.evidence: The arity condition exempts every len call. len() reaches args[0] in code generation and raises IndexError; len(a, 999) compiles and silently ignores the extra argument.
findings.impact: Bad source crashes the compiler or has an argument silently ignored.
findings.recommendation: Require exactly one argument and validate it before code generation. Ensure compiler errors are reported as VErr rather than Python exceptions.

findings.title: print does not preserve integer signedness or wide float values
findings.evidence: emit_print sends every 8-bit integer to put_char, so i8 value -1 emits byte 0xff instead of decimal -1. u64 value 18446744073709551615 prints -1 because put_int accepts i64. put_float converts the integral part to i64, so printing 1e20 produces -9223372036854775808.000000.
findings.impact: The documented print operation corrupts the textual value of supported integer and floating-point types.
findings.recommendation: Format signed and unsigned integers according to their actual types, and format f64 without narrowing its integral part to i64. Make character output explicit: char is currently an alias of u8, so distinguishing it automatically requires a type-model change.

findings.title: exp has much lower accuracy than its documented claim
findings.evidence: The function sums only terms 0 through 13 of the Taylor series. exp(4.9) printed 134.212425; the reference value is 134.28977968493552, far from the comment's claimed approximately 1e-12 accuracy for |x| < 5.
findings.impact: Ordinary inputs produce a visible error, and the approximation becomes worse outside the stated range.
findings.recommendation: Use range reduction plus a bounded approximation, or clearly document and test the supported range and error bound.

findings.title: hypot overflows while squaring finite inputs
findings.evidence: The implementation directly evaluates sqrt(x*x + y*y), despite the comment promising no overflow. Inputs around 1e200 overflow the intermediate squares although the mathematical result is finite.
findings.impact: hypot returns infinity or an unusable value for large but valid finite arguments.
findings.recommendation: Scale by the larger absolute input before squaring, or use a standard hypot implementation if one is linked.

findings.title: Descending range behavior depends on whether bounds are literals
findings.evidence: The compiler selects descending iteration only when both bounds are integer literals. for i in 3..0 iterated 3, 2, 1, while equivalent variable bounds produced an empty loop. The language reference describes ranges as [a, b).
findings.impact: Replacing a literal with a variable changes the loop's behavior.
findings.recommendation: Implement the documented ascending half-open rule (i < stop) for all bound expressions. If descending ranges are intended as an extension, document and test that rule independently of AST shape.

findings.title: Duplicate struct definitions are silently ignored
findings.evidence: The duplicate check only raises when the existing entry is not a StructDef, but the first pass stores StructDef values. Two definitions named X therefore compile and the first definition wins; a constructor matching the second definition can be checked against the wrong fields.
findings.impact: A declaration error is hidden and later code may use an unintended struct layout.
findings.recommendation: Raise on every repeated struct name, while allowing only explicitly supported forward declarations. Add a duplicate-definition test.

findings.title: A struct constructor is accepted as an argument but cannot be lowered
findings.evidence: The type checker accepts take(Point(7)) as a struct-valued argument, but call_gen asks eaddr for the constructor expression and code generation reports that a struct constructor is not addressable.
findings.impact: A type-correct expression fails late in code generation instead of compiling or receiving an early semantic error.
findings.recommendation: Materialize constructor arguments into temporary storage before passing them, or reject them during type checking with a precise diagnostic.

findings.title: Standard output and error helpers ignore partial writes
findings.evidence: put_str, put_int, put_err, and put_errnl issue single write syscalls and ignore the returned count. Linux write may write fewer bytes than requested or return EINTR, especially for large output or pipes.
findings.impact: Long stdout/stderr strings and numeric buffers can be truncated without an error being reported.
findings.recommendation: Add a write_all loop that advances by the returned count, handles EINTR, and reports other errors. Use it for standard output and error helpers.

findings.title: Concurrent compiler runs share temporary build artifacts
findings.evidence: The CLI uses a process-specific assembly path but every build still overwrites /tmp/opencode/volt_rt.o. The compile_src default also reuses volt_build.s, its object file, and volt_build.bin, so concurrent calls through that API collide across build artifacts.
findings.impact: Parallel builds can overwrite an object while another linker is reading it, causing flaky build failures or corrupted outputs.
findings.recommendation: Create a unique temporary build directory per compilation and keep all generated assembly, object, and executable files inside it.

findings.title: The test runner can hang indefinitely and update mode can bless failures
findings.evidence: Each test subprocess has no timeout. With --update, the runner writes captured output even when compilation or execution returned nonzero.
findings.impact: A looping regression hangs the suite; an accidental --update can replace a good golden file with an error result.
findings.recommendation: Set a per-test timeout, handle TimeoutExpired, and refuse to update golden output when compilation or execution fails unless an explicit force option is used.

findings.title: By-value recursive structs are accepted with an invalid layout
findings.evidence: resolve_struct registers an unfinished TStruct before resolving fields. A direct field of the same struct sees size zero during layout, so struct Node { next: Node } compiles instead of being rejected as infinitely recursive.
findings.impact: The declared field has no valid finite storage layout; member access and copies do not represent the declared type.
findings.recommendation: Track structs currently being resolved and reject by-value recursion. Continue to allow recursion through ptr<Node>.

improvement_suggestions.recommendation: Add negative tests for malformed syntax, duplicate definitions, type mismatches, bad builtin arity, invalid native assembly, and ABI limits. Assert a concise compiler diagnostic rather than a Python traceback.
Array bounds checks are explicitly absent. Consider an optional checked build mode for indexing and pointer arithmetic, with tests for empty, first, and one-past-end indices.

Generated binaries currently have no PT_GNU_STACK program header. Emit a .note.GNU-stack marker in generated and runtime assembly, then verify the resulting stack policy on supported Linux toolchains.
powi and ipowi use one multiplication per exponent step. Exponentiation by squaring reduces large exponents from O(n) to O(log n), with explicit handling for INT64_MIN and negative exponents.

Clarify whether module-level let values are mutable after constant initialization; the compiler permits functions to assign them although the reference calls them constants. Document the 1 MiB string arena limit and panic behavior as well.

Remove unused helpers and state such as str_escape, the unused local p in str_arena_new, BUILTIN_VA, IRMAP, and the no-op loop assignment in typecheck_fn. Keep refactoring separate from correctness fixes.

not_checked: Git history and a change diff are unavailable because this directory is not a Git repository.
The snake example was inspected but not interactively tested in a real terminal.
The report does not claim compatibility with non-Linux or non-x86-64 targets; those are documented as unsupported.
verdict: Historical verdict for the pre-0.3.0 tree. VOLT 0.3.0 now checks safe arrays, strings, integer arithmetic, and numeric conversions; raw pointers remain explicitly unsafe and are not sandboxed.
